summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of Britannia Industries' Q1 FY27 results, accurately capturing the key themes of volume recovery and margin pressures. However, some specific financial figures are illustrative and differ from official reports.

claims.claim: Britannia Industries' Q1 FY27 results indicate an easing of the dual-pricing issue, leading to improved sales volumes.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the easing of dual-pricing and its positive impact on volumes.

claims.claim: The company reported a consolidated revenue from operations of an illustrative ₹4,450 crores, marking a healthy year-on-year growth of approximately 9.5%.
claims.note: Consolidated revenue from operations for Q1 FY27 was reported as ₹4,964 crore (9.5% YoY growth) or ₹5,000 crore (8.2% YoY growth) by various sources, not ₹4,450 crores.

claims.claim: Illustrative net profit for the quarter stood at around ₹570 crores, reflecting a modest year-on-year increase of about 6.0%.
claims.note: Consolidated net profit for Q1 FY27 was reported as ₹591 crore (13.6% YoY increase) or ₹593.38 crore (14.08% YoY increase) by various sources, not ₹570 crores and 6.0% increase.

claims.claim: Consequently, the company witnessed a commendable volume growth of around 8% year-on-year, which translated into market share gains in its core biscuit categories.
claims.note: Volume growth was reported as approximately 9% year-on-year.

claims.claim: For instance, wheat flour, a primary ingredient, saw an illustrative price increase of 7-8% year-on-year, while sugar prices also remained elevated.
claims.note: Wheat flour costs actually declined 7% versus Q1 FY26. Sugar prices did remain elevated.

claims.claim: Britannia's gross margins, which contracted by an illustrative 120 basis points year-on-year to approximately 39.5%.
claims.note: While input costs impacted margins, a specific gross margin figure of 39.5% and a 120 basis point contraction were not explicitly found in the provided search results. Some sources mention profit from operations as a percentage of sales reached 15.3% and PAT at 11.9%.

claims.claim: Illustrative A&P expenses as a percentage of sales rose to about 3.5% from 2.8% in the year-ago period.
claims.note: Sources confirm increased A&P spends impacted EBITDA, but specific percentages (3.5% from 2.8%) were not found.

claims.claim: The Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortisation (EBITDA) margin for Q1 FY27 stood at an illustrative 15.2%, down from 16.5% in the corresponding quarter last year.
claims.note: EBITDA margins were reported as almost flat at 16.8% in Q1 FY27 versus 16.4% in the year-ago period, or profit from operations at 15.3%.

article_title: Britannia's Q1 FY27: Easing Concerns, Navigating Costs
